expected_sources.role: Restructuring paper with the explanation of delays

text: Latest disclosed ISR: sequence 8, ISR07766, archived 15 June 2026. Targets are end-of-project targets (May or November 2028).

PDO indicators, all at 0 against target (pp. 3-4): beneficiaries with improved water services 0 of 1,600,000 (female 0 of 752,000; refugees 0 of 80,000; host communities 0 of 480,000); volume of NRW reduction 0 of 7,000,000 m3/year; electricity use reduced 0 of 60 GWh/year; drought management system 0 of 4 components operationalized.

Intermediate indicators (pp. 4-7): women certified as plumbers 20 of 550 (first training in May 2026); km of networks and reservoirs rehabilitated or replaced 0 of 1,500; DMAs with NRW foundations 0 (target revised in March 2026); renewable energy capacity 0 of 25 MW; drought bulletins, annual water allocation plans, drought contingency plans and dam rehabilitation assessments all 0; utility performance and NRW systems PBC indicators 'No'.
Performance-based conditions (pp. 7-8): only the dam risk-indexing PBC is recorded as achieved; the others are not yet achieved or not due.

Explanations in the ISR: very little. The key-issues note says the March-April 2026 mission saw moderate improvement in the pace of implementation and procurement, with consultancy contracts awarded and more key contracts expected in calendar 2026 (p. 2). Ratings: PDO Moderately Satisfactory, implementation Moderately Unsatisfactory, risk Moderate (p. 1). Disbursement 3.86% of the IBRD loan (p. 9).

The fuller explanation is in the March 2026 restructuring paper: detailed designs did not exist at appraisal, so design-and-supervision consultants had to be hired before works; Component 2 procurement was slow for capacity reasons; PBC achievements had not yet been verified (pp. 6-7).
